officialTitle: First-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab in unresectable malignant pleural mesothelioma (CheckMate 743): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Between Nov 29, 2016, and April 28, 2018, 713 patients were enrolled, of whom 605 were randomly assigned to either nivolumab plus ipilimumab (n=303) or chemotherapy (n=302).
design.notes: ECOG PS 0-1; 103 hospitals in 21 countries. Prespecified interim analysis reported in the primary publication; 3-year update and patient-reported outcomes published separately.

clinicalQuestion: Does first-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab improve overall survival over platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy in unresectable pleural mesothelioma?

pico.population: Previously untreated, unresectable malignant pleural mesothelioma, ECOG PS 0-1
pico.intervention: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every 6 weeks for up to 2 years
pico.comparator: Pemetrexed plus cisplatin or carboplatin every 3 weeks for up to six cycles
pico.outcomes: Primary: OS. Secondary: PFS, ORR, safety; patient-reported outcomes

arms.label: Nivolumab + ipilimumab
arms.dosing: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV every 6 weeks for up to 2 years
arms.doseSourceQuote: Eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to nivolumab (3 mg/kg intravenously once every 2 weeks) plus ipilimumab (1 mg/kg intravenously once every 6 weeks) for up to 2 years

arms.label: Chemotherapy
arms.dosing: Pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 plus cisplatin 75 mg/m2 or carboplatin AUC 5 every 3 weeks for up to six cycles
arms.doseSourceQuote: or platinum plus pemetrexed chemotherapy (pemetrexed [500 mg/mintravenously] plus cisplatin [75 mg/mintravenously] or carboplatin [area under the concentration-time curve 5 mg/mL per min intravenously]) once every 3 weeks for up to six cycles.

publications.title: First-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab in unresectable malignant pleural mesothelioma (CheckMate 743): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial.
publications.label: Prespecified interim analysis

publications.title: First-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus chemotherapy in patients with unresectable malignant pleural mesothelioma: 3-year outcomes from CheckMate 743.
publications.label: 3-year update

publications.title: First-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus chemotherapy for the treatment of unresectable malignant pleural mesothelioma: patient-reported outcomes in CheckMate 743.
publications.label: Patient-reported outcomes

outcomes.sourceQuote: At the prespecified interim analysis (database lock April 3, 2020; median follow-up of 29·7 months [IQR 26·7-32·9]), nivolumab plus ipilimumab significantly extended overall survival versus chemotherapy (median overall survival 18·1 months [95% CI 16·8-21·4] vs 14·1 months [12·4-16·2]; hazard ratio 0·74 [96·6% CI 0·60-0·91]; p=0·0020).
2-year overall survival rates were 41% (95% CI 35·1-46·5) in the nivolumab plus ipilimumab group and 27% (21·9-32·4) in the chemotherapy group.

With a median follow-up of 43.1 months, nivolumab plus ipilimumab continued to prolong OS versus chemotherapy. Median OS was 18.1 versus 14.1 months [hazard ratio (95% confidence interval), 0.73 (0.61-0.87)], and 3-year OS rates were 23% versus 15%, respectively.
Three-year progression-free survival rates were 14% versus 1%, and objective response rates were 40% versus 44%.
Three-year progression-free survival rates were 14% versus 1%, and objective response rates were 40% versus 44%. At 3 years, 28% versus 0% of responders had an ongoing response.

outcomes.endpointLabel: Time to definitive deterioration in HRQoL
outcomes.sourceQuote: Nivolumab + ipilimumab delayed time to definitive deterioration in HRQoL (hazard ratio 0.52 [95% confidence interval 0.36-0.74]) and showed a trend in symptom delay versus chemotherapy.

safety.sourceQuote: Grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were reported in 91 (30%) of 300 patients treated with nivolumab plus ipilimumab and 91 (32%) of 284 treated with chemotherapy.
Three (1%) treatment-related deaths occurred in the nivolumab plus ipilimumab group (pneumonitis, encephalitis, and heart failure) and one (<1%) in the chemotherapy group (myelosuppression).

strengths: Large international randomised phase III trial with OS primary endpoint
limitations: Response rate was not higher than chemotherapy; benefit is driven by durability
Histology-specific benefit is based on subgroup analyses

clinicalImplications.text: Established first-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab as a chemotherapy-free standard for unresectable pleural mesothelioma, with durable survival benefit and maintained quality of life; the authors report benefit regardless of histology.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Response rates are similar to chemotherapy, but responses are more durable; do not judge dual checkpoint blockade by early response alone.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from PubMed abstracts of PMIDs 33485464 (primary), 35124183 (3-year update) and 35367910 (patient-reported outcomes). Histology-specific subgroup results were not transcribed because the abstracts report them qualitatively.
